extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent attorneys, applicants, and IP office officials in Argentina
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory rules and administrative/procedural requirements for obtaining, enforcing, transferring, and forfeiting invention patents and utility model certificates in the Argentine Republic under Law No. 24.481 (as amended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (Article 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions relating to products or processes shall be patentable, provided that they are new, that they involve an inventive activity and that they are susceptible of industrial application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes definitions: (a) invention = human creation enabling transformation of matter or energy for exploitation; (b) novel = not included in the state of the art; (c) state of the art = totality of technical knowledge publicly disclosed before filing/priority date; (d) inventive activity = cannot be readily deduced by an average skilled person; (e) industrial applicability = produces an industrial result (industry broadly defined including agriculture, services). (Article 4 a–e).

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year disclosure grace (Article 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of an invention shall not affect its novelty, as long as within one (1) year prior to the filing date (or priority date) the inventor or successors made the invention known by any means or displayed it at an exhibition, accompanied by documentary supporting evidence as regulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must supply documentary evidence under regulations; applies to inventor/self-disclosures and exhibition displays within 12 months before filing/priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-inventions / excluded subject matter (Article 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following shall not be considered inventions: discoveries, scientific theories and mathematical methods; literary or artistic works; schemes, rules or methods for intellectual activities, games, economic/business activities and computer programs; forms of data presentation; methods of surgical, therapeutic or diagnostic treatment applicable to the human body or relating to animals; mere juxtaposition/obvious modifications of known items except in specified combination cases; any kind of living matter or substances already existing in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists subject-matter exclusions and clarifies that combinations which render components unable to function separately or produce non-obvious industrial results may be patentable (Article 6 f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public order / morality and biological material exclusions (Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not patentable: (a) inventions whose exploitation on Argentine territory is to be prevented to protect public good/morality/health/life/plants/environment; (b) all biological and genetic material existing in nature or their replicas and biological processes implicit in reproduction including self-duplicating material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy-based exclusions including natural biological material and reproductive biological processes (Article 7 a–b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to a patent / owner’s exclusive rights (Article 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent confers on its owner the exclusive rights: (a) for product patents, to prevent third parties from manufacture, use, offering for sale, sale or importation without consent; (b) for process patents, to prevent utilization of the process and acts concerning the product obtained directly by the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines scope of exclusionary rights; subject to Articles 36 and 99 exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of inventorship (Article 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of proof to the contrary, persons designated as inventors in the application shall be presumed to be the inventors and have the right to be mentioned in the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant entries of inventor name carry evidentiary weight unless rebutted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee inventions / ownership and remuneration (Article 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions made by a worker in the course of contract/employment where the object is the performance of inventive activity belong to the employer; worker may be entitled to additional remuneration if contribution and importance exceed contract terms; employer may claim ownership when invention connected to professional activity and influenced by company knowledge/means (must exercise option within 90 days); workers entitled to fair economic compensation; inventions filed within one (1) year after leaving employment are considered developed during the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when employer ownership applies, rights to extra compensation, option exercise period (90 days), and prohibition of advance waiver by worker (null and void). (Article 10 a–f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims determine scope of patent rights (Article 11 & 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first of the approved claims determines the right conferred and defines/demarcates scope; claims shall define the subject matter, be clear and concise, be based on the description without exceeding it; first claim refers to main subject matter and the remainder are subordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims interpreted with description, drawings, plans, or biological deposit where applicable. Claims must not extend beyond description (Article 11, 22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements and formalities for priority (Articles 12–15, 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed with the National Patent Administration must include characteristics and data as Law/regulations indicate; a patent may be applied for by inventor/successors/representative; priority date is date of first application abroad if within one (1) year; priority must be claimed at filing and may require priority document and Spanish translation; several inventors — right belongs to earliest filing (first-to-file). Filing date requires: declaration of application, applicant identity, description and one or more claims (even if not formally compliant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority partial if Argentine application is broader than foreign one; reciprocity required in country of first application; Administration may request priority document during substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (Article 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent application may not comprise more than one invention or group of inventions so related as to constitute a single general inventive concept; non-complying applications shall be divided as regulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-unity leads to mandatory divisional filings as per regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum content at filing / 30-day cure period (Articles 18–19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing date requires basic declaration, applicant identity, a description and one or more claims even if not formally compliant. For grant, must file name/description, plans or technical drawings, claims, and an abstract for publication; failure to supply these within thirty (30) days from filing causes refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant has 30 days to supply missing formal items or application is refused without further processing (Article 19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of disclosure / best mode / enablement (Article 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must be described with sufficient clarity and completeness for an average skilled person to carry it out; must include clear account of best known method and materials; methods/processes described shall be directly applicable in production; for microorganisms, deposit and access requirements apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes requirement of deposit for strains in authorized institution and public access conditions after publication; description is used to interpret claims and must enable reproduction by skilled person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings clarity (Article 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting drawings, plans and diagrams must be sufficiently clear for the description to be understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical drawings are part of disclosure and must aid comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between patent and utility model (Article 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application may be converted into a utility model application and vice versa within thirty (30) days from filing or within thirty (30) days from conversion requirement by the Administration; failure to convert within term = abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-act conversion deadlines; conversion possible during processing per specified terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examination and correction requests (Article 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: National Patent Administration will conduct preliminary examination and may request specification/clarification or correction of errors or omissions; applicant must comply within thirty (30) days or application is considered abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration may seek clarifications; non-compliance leads to abandonment; preliminary examination distinct from substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and publication timing (Articles 25–26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending patent application and annexes remain confidential until publication. Administration shall publish pending applications within eighteen (18) months from filing; applicant may request earlier publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication triggers public access and third-party objections period (Article 28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination fee requirement (Article 27)
rubrics_metrics.description: On payment of a fee established by implementing Decree, the Administration will carry out substantive examination to determine compliance with patentability criteria; failing to pay within 18 months from filing = application considered withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration may request copies of foreign substantive examinations and reports from researchers; applicant may request on-site examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office actions / applicant response periods (Article 28)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where application calls for comment, Administration notifies applicant so that within sixty (60) days they may provide clarifications or requested information; failure to comply = application withdrawn. All comments are made in one single act unless prior clarifications requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties may raise objections within sixty (60) days from publication, based on non-fulfillment or insufficient fulfillment of legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection and notification (Article 29)
rubrics_metrics.description: If comments are not satisfactorily addressed, the application shall be rejected with written notification stating reasons and arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant receives reasoned written decision allowing appeal as provided elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant and publication of patent (Articles 30 & 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where requirements have been met, the Administration shall grant the title; grant shall be published on the Institute website per enforcement authority ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant does not prejudice third-party claims to stronger rights and carries no State guarantee of usefulness (Article 31). Only material/formal error corrections allowed in granted title (Article 33).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term (Article 35)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent has a non-renewable term of twenty (20) years from the filing date of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term measured from filing; utility models have different term (Article 54).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights exceptions — experimental, medical compounding, exhaustion, accidental use (Article 36)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent rights have no effect against: (a) third parties conducting private/academic non-commercial experimental/teaching activities that manufacture/use the product/process; (b) routine preparation of medicines by authorized professionals individually on prescription; (c) any person who acquires/uses/imports/markets the patented product once lawfully placed on the market in any country (exhaustion); (d) use on board foreign vehicles temporarily in Argentina.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates common statutory exceptions including research/experimental use and national exhaustion ties to TRIPS reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferability, registration and formalities for assignment (Articles 37 & 38)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents and utility models are transferable and may be licensed; to bind third parties, assignment must be registered before the National Institute of Industrial Property. License agreements shall not contain restrictive trade clauses affecting production, marketing, technological development, competition or impose prohibited conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits clauses preventing challenges to validity, mandatory transfer-back, mandatory joint licenses, and other anti-competitive practices (Article 38).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-exclusivity of licenses by default (Article 39)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided, granting a license does not exclude possibility of owner granting other licenses or exploiting the invention themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presumption of non-exclusivity unless contract stipulates exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee enforcement rights (Article 40)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiary of a contractual license has right to bring legal actions available to owner only where owner does not bring them himself/herself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee's enforcement contingent on owner inactivity per statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative exceptions to patent rights (Article 41)
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Institute may, at reasoned request of competent authority, introduce limited exceptions to patent rights provided they do not unjustifiably prejudice normal exploitation or harm legitimate patent-owner interests, bearing in mind third-party legitimate interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framework for administrative carve-outs balancing owner and public/third-party interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licensing for failure to work (Articles 42–43)
rubrics_metrics.description: If prospective user has attempted to obtain a license on reasonable commercial terms and failed within 150 days, the Institute may allow other uses without owner authorization. Also, after 3 years from grant or 4 from filing, if invention not exploited (except force majeure) or preparations not made, or exploitation interrupted >1 year, any person may apply for authorization to use patent without owner's permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines force majeure (technical/legal difficulties like regulatory delays; lack of funds/economic viability alone not sufficient). Owner notified of non-fulfillment before authorization; remuneration decided by implementing authority after hearing parties; decisions within ninety (90) working days; appeals to Civil and Commercial Federal Courts, no suspensive effect on appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticompetitive practices as grounds for use without authorization (Article 44)
rubrics_metrics.description: Right to use without owner authorization may be granted where the owner engaged in anticompetitive practices (e.g., excessive prices, refusal to supply on reasonable terms, slowing production/marketing, other punishable practices under Law No. 22.262).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases grant can be effected without applying Article 42 procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government use / emergency exploitation (Article 45)
rubrics_metrics.description: National Executive Power may, for sanitary emergency or national security reasons, order exploitation of certain patents by granting exploitation rights; scope/duration limited to purposes of grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory basis for government-use licenses in emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent patents / cross-licensing conditions (Article 46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use without owner authorization may be granted to exploit a second patent that cannot be worked without infringing a first patent provided: (a) second patent represents significant technical progress of considerable economic importance over first; (b) first patent owner entitled to cross-licensing on reasonable terms; (c) authorized use of first patent cannot be assigned without assignment of second patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses improvement patents and blocking patents; cross-licensing and assignment tied to dependency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization observance (Article 47)
rubrics_metrics.description: When uses without owner authorization are allowed, authorization given by Institute, considered per case circumstances; authorizations extend to components/process patents necessary to exploit patent; uses non-exclusive; may not be assigned except with business asset; supply mainly domestic market; owner receives reasonable remuneration; limitations on duration and scope, special rules for semiconductors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies conditions for compulsory licenses and remuneration assessment; semiconductors restricted to non-commercial public use or remedies for anticompetitive practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review and appeal (Articles 48–49)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions relating to uses not authorized by owner are subject to judicial review including remuneration matters; appeals against administrative acts connected with authorization have no suspensive effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative decisions can be reviewed by courts, and appeals do not stay effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic capability requirement for applicant for compulsory use (Article 50)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person applying for uses contemplated (compulsory licensing) must possess economic ability to carry out efficient exploitation and have premises authorized by competent authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must demonstrate capacity to exploit licensed patent effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents of addition / improvement patents (Articles 51–52)
rubrics_metrics.description: Person who improves a patented invention may apply for a patent of addition which is granted for the remainder of the lifespan of the main patent; where multiple additions exist, the one expiring last is considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additions expire with main patent; conversion/independence rules if main patent invalidated (Article 61).

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model eligibility and definition (Article 53)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new arrangement or form in tools, instruments, utensils, devices or known objects suitable for practical work that improves performance confers exploitation rights via utility model certificate; certificate granted only to new form/arrangement and not where scope is that of an in-force invention patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility models protect practical improvements to known objects; cannot overlap with existing invention patent protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model term and fees (Article 54)
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility model certificates valid for ten (10) non-extendable years from filing date and subject to fees per implementing Decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate term from invention patents; substantive examination fee rules apply (Article 57).

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model requisites and application content (Articles 55–57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Essential requisites: inventions under Title III must be new and industrial in nature. Application must include title, description of single main instance of new configuration or arrangement and explanation of causal relationship to functional improvement sufficient for skilled person to reproduce, claims, and necessary drawings. After filing and substantive exam fee payment, Administration examines compliance and publishes if approved; 30-day post-publication objection window; failure to pay substantive exam fee within three (3) months from filing = abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility model objections must be reasoned and based on lack/insufficiency of legal requisites; examination and publication process similar to patents but quicker and with different time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity and partial invalidity (Articles 59–61)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents and utility models are wholly or partly null and void when granted in violation of the Law. If invalidity affects only part, partial invalidity declared by cancellation of affected claim(s); a claim cannot be declared partially invalid. Invalidation of patent does not automatically invalidate additions; conversion of additions into independent patents may be applied for within ninety (90) days after notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural consequences for invalidity including claim cancellation and preservation of unaffected claims; conversion window for dependent patents of addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes of lapse (Article 62)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents and utility models lapse on expiration of term; renunciation by owner (joint if multiple owners); failure to pay annual maintenance fees (with 180-day grace period except force majeure); where a licensee is granted and invention not worked within two (2) years for reasons attributable to owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative decision declaring lapse subject to judicial appeal with no suspensive effect; grace period for fees and force majeure exceptions relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public domain effect without judicial declaration (Article 63)
rubrics_metrics.description: No judicial declaration necessary for invalidity or lapse to make invention public property; invalidity and lapse take effect automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court decision not required to free invention; administrative determinations have effect per statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing to bring invalidity/lapse actions (Article 64)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person with legitimate interest may bring action for invalidation or lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad standing allows third parties to challenge validity or lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative proceedings fee/payment and representation statements (Articles 67–69)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications subject to payment of filing fee; failure to pay = rejection. Representation capacity invoked in applications has force of sworn statement; Administration may request documentation; business manager capacity must be ratified within forty (40) working days or application abandoned. Applicant must elect legal domicile within territory and notify any amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal and timing requirements for fees and representation; ratification periods enforced to prevent abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to pending files and confidentiality of staff (Article 70)
rubrics_metrics.description: Until publication, pending files may be consulted only by applicant, legal representative, or authorized persons; staff processing applications obliged to keep file contents confidential, except official information or that required by judicial authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-publication confidentiality protections and limited access exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-employment restriction for Institute employees (Article 71)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees of the National Institute may not directly or indirectly process rights on behalf of third parties until two (2) years after employment cessation, on pain of dismissal and fine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflict of interest / revolving-door restriction to preserve impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative appeal timelines (Articles 72–74)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative appeal against decision refusing patent or utility model must be lodged in writing with President of the Institute within an absolute period of thirty (30) working days from notification; appeal accompanied by supporting documentation; Institute issues decision after analysis; unfavorable decisions are notified; favorable decisions follow grant publication procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict 30-working-day deadline; appeal is administrative internal review step prior to judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal and civil remedies for infringement (Articles 75–81)
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringement treated as counterfeiting punishable by imprisonment of six (6) months to three (3) years and a fine. Same penalties for producing, importing, selling, marketing infringing objects; increased penalties for insiders who appropriate/disclose before protection; fines for misleading use of patent indications; repeat offenses double penalty. In addition to criminal actions, owner/licensee may bring civil actions to prohibit unlawful exploitation and claim compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal and civil enforcement available; aggravated penalties for insider misconduct and repeated offenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precautionary/preliminary measures criteria (Article 83)
rubrics_metrics.description: On submission of patent/certificate, injured party may seek precautionary measures (seizure of samples, inventory/embargo of articles/machines). Judges may order preliminary measures to prevent infringement and preserve evidence if: (a) likelihood that patent if challenged will be declared valid; (b) summarily proven delay would cause irreparable prejudice to patentee; (c) prejudice to patentee exceeds prejudice to alleged infringer if measures wrongly granted; (d) reasonable likelihood that patent is being infringed. In exceptional cases risk of evidence destruction permits inaudita altera parte orders; expert must pronounce on (a) and (d) within fifteen (15) days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may require bond or guarantee from plaintiff to protect defendant and avoid excesses; preliminary measures executed by Court Officer with expert assistance; measures lapse if plaintiff fails to bring appropriate legal action within fifteen (15) days (Article 86).

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution / evidentiary procedures and defendant obligations (Articles 84–88)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures carried out by Court Officer with expert(s); persons with infringing goods must provide full account of source/quantity/value/time of sales or be considered accomplices. Where subject matter is a process, Judges shall order defendant to prove that process used is different; Judges may order plaintiff to prove infringement if product from patented process is not new. Protection of defendants' trade secrets considered when providing evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifts evidentiary burdens depending on whether product is new or identical and balances secrecy interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for civil and criminal actions (Article 89)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal judges in Civil and Commercial Matters competent for civil suits (ordinary proceedings); Federal judges in Criminal and Correctional Matters competent for penal actions (correctional procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies forum competence for enforcement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and powers of National Institute of Industrial Property (Articles 90–95)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates National Institute as implementing authority under Ministry of Economy and Public Works; lists assets, governance (President and Vice-president appointed by National Executive with four-year terms), Control Office, duties (ensure observance, hire staff, enter agreements, establish/modify fees, publish registers, create databank, simplify grant procedures), Board functions (propose amendments, issue guidelines, budget control, hold contests, appoint directors/registrars, hear appeals, grant licenses under Title II Chapter VIII), and creation of National Patent Administration department headed by Commissioner and Under-commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative/political organization and delegations for patent system implementation and policy; includes duty to simplify procedures and adapt to new technologies (Article 92 k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations, fees, and implementing Decree powers (Articles 96 & 104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing Decree shall set amounts of fines, annual fees, charges and specify method of adjusting them; National Executive shall issue regulations under this Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation to executive for procedural and fee details; fees referenced throughout (e.g., substantive examination, maintenance fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional provisions for pharmaceutical patents (Articles 100–101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions relating to pharmaceutical products shall not be patentable until five (5) years have elapsed following publication of this Law; patent applications for pharmaceuticals may be filed but patents shall be granted only as from five (5) years after publication; patent owner has exclusive rights from five-year date with special provisions about remuneration where third parties use invention before owner-exclusive period, and TRIPS compliance may require amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary moratorium on pharmaceutical product patents with specified grandfathering and remuneration provisions; implementation harmonized with WTO/TRIPS obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing abroad pre-enactment rule (Article 102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications filed abroad prior to enactment whose subject matter was not patentable under prior law but is under this Law may be filed domestically if: (a) first application filed within year preceding enactment; (b) applicant proves foreign filing per Decree; (c) exploitation/importation hasn't started on a commercial scale; (d) validity ends same date as in country of first application provided 20-year term not exceeded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional allowance for foreign-filed applications with conditions and term alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication exception for pending pre-existing applications (Article 99)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions on publication of applications (Article 26) shall not apply to patent applications pending on date of Law's entry into force; such patents need only be published as provided in Article 32.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grandfathering of pre-existing pending applications regarding publication rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal limits on title amendments (Article 33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only changes to the text of the patent title aimed to correct material or formal errors may be introduced after grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-grant amendment scope limited to corrections; substantive change prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees, grace period, and lapse effect (Article 62 c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to pay annual maintenance fees leads to lapse; owner has grace period of one hundred and eighty (180) days to pay updated fee, except where non-payment due to force majeure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines administrative lapse procedure and grace period; force majeure exceptions possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment rules and conversion failure consequences (Articles 16, 23, 24, 57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may abandon application at any time; where application belongs to more than one applicant abandonment must be joint or rights accrue to remaining applicants. Failure to convert within stipulated term or to respond to Administration requests within prescribed periods results in abandonment. For utility models, failure to pay substantive exam fee within three (3) months from filing = abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple provisions set strict time-limited cure/response windows; failure results in abandonment with procedural consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication triggers opposition/objection windows (Articles 26 & 28 & 57)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication within 18 months (or earlier on request) triggers a sixty (60)-day opposition period during which any person may raise reasoned objections with documentary proof against patent applications; utility model publication triggers a thirty (30)-day objection window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different objection windows: patents 60 days after publication; utility models 30 days. Objections must be based on non-fulfillment or insufficiency of legal requisites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence deposit and access for microorganisms (Article 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: For microorganism-related applications, the strain must be deposited in an authorized institution; the public shall have access to the microorganism culture at the depository as from publication under conditions established by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes deposit obligation and public access regime for biological material disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural confidentiality exceptions (Article 70)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidentiality does not apply to information of official character or that may be required by judicial authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits to confidentiality during pendency to accommodate official and judicial needs.
